PART 1 - the action script scripts/operator/actions/v3-derived-lifecycle-status.sh. Model it line-for-line on v3-derived-data-status.sh: bash prologue that locates CPython 3.14 (python3.14, else python3 that proves CPython 3.14) and emits the same 'stopped' JSON receipt on failure; then `exec "$PYTHON_BIN" - <<'PY'` with the Python body. Keep: EXPECTED_HOST = "ed-finder-prod", EXPECTED_FQDN = "nb79a3d.mevnode.com", POSTGRES_CONTAINER = "edfinder-v3-phase4c-full-20260827_r5-postgres", the pwd -P == /opt/ed-finder check, resolve_database_identity() reading ONLY $POSTGRES_USER and ${POSTGRES_DB:-$POSTGRES_USER} from inside the container, psql() wrapping every statement in BEGIN READ ONLY + SET LOCAL statement_timeout + COMMIT with -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1, run() with a process timeout, and the receipt skeleton {schema_version 'ed-finder/operator-operation-result/v1', operation 'v3-derived-lifecycle-status', status, read_only True, direct_db_access_performed, db_writes_performed False, env_files_read False, private_keys_read False, service_changes_performed False, filesystem_writes_performed False, database_identity_source, query_policy}. STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS = 20000. Every SQL statement is hard-coded; no user input reaches SQL. Output is ONE line of compact JSON (json.dumps sort_keys=True separators=(',',':')) and the exit code is 0 only when there are no failures.
The receipt must contain these sections, in addition to host/postgres identity:
(a) 'workers': for each of exactly these container names, in this order — edfinder-ratings-v4-prod-p4, edfinder-ratings-v4-prod-p4-opt1, edfinder-ratings-v4-prod-p4-parallel-v1, edfinder-v3-system-search-p4-opt1 — run `docker inspect -f '{{.State.Status}}\t{{.State.Running}}\t{{.State.ExitCode}}\t{{.State.FinishedAt}}' <name>` and record {name, exists (bool), running (bool or null), status (str or null), exit_code (int or null), finished_at (str or null)}; a missing container is exists=false, running=false, NOT a failure. Then 'all_named_workers_stopped': true iff no listed worker has running=true. A running worker is reported, not treated as a failure (status stays 'success'); the caller decides.
(b) 'schema_migrations': every row of v3_meta.schema_migration ordered by applied_at then migration_name: {migration_name, migration_sha256_hex (encode(migration_sha256,'hex')), applied_at (::text)}. Also 'finder_migrations_applied': {'010_v3_system_search_body_type_counts.sql': bool, '011_v3_system_archetype.sql': bool, '013_v3_system_search_parallel.sql': bool, '014_v3_watchlist.sql': bool} computed from that list (use the exact file names found in sql/v3/migration-manifest.txt and sql/v3/migrations/ for 010/011/013/014; if a name differs from these, use the real one and say so in your summary).
(c) 'canonical': current pointer from v3_meta.current_canonical_generation joined to v3_meta.canonical_generation: {generation_id, generation_key, relation_schema, lifecycle_state, publication_sequence, published_at}; null when the pointer table is empty. Plus 'canonical_generations': every v3_meta.canonical_generation row ordered by created_at: {generation_id, generation_key, lifecycle_state, created_at, published_at, retired_at, failed_at, failure_reason (first 240 chars or null)}.
(d) 'derived': current pointer from v3_meta.current_derived_generation joined to v3_meta.derived_generation: {derived_generation_id, generation_key, lifecycle_state, canonical_generation_id, publication_sequence, published_at}; null when empty. Plus 'derived_generations': every v3_meta.derived_generation row ordered by created_at: {derived_generation_id, generation_key, canonical_generation_id, canonical_publication_sequence, mechanics_version, scorer_version, adapter_version, lifecycle_state, expected_systems, expected_bodies, created_at, validated_at, published_at, failed_at, failure (first 240 chars or null)}.
(e) 'derived_products': every v3_meta.derived_product row joined to derived_generation for generation_key, ordered by generation created_at, product_code: {derived_generation_id, generation_key, product_code, product_version, lifecycle_state, expected_rows, created_at, validated_at, failed_at, failure (first 240 chars or null), validation_sha256_hex (or null)}. If to_regclass('v3_meta.derived_product') is NULL (migration 006 absent) record 'derived_products': null and 'derived_product_table_present': false instead of failing.
(f) 'spatial': if to_regclass('v3_spatial.current_spatial_generation') is NULL record {'present': false}; else the pointer joined to v3_spatial.spatial_generation: {spatial_generation_id, canonical_generation_id, pyramid_version, lifecycle_state, publication_sequence, published_at} (null pointer when empty) plus 'spatial_generations': every v3_spatial.spatial_generation row ordered by created_at: {spatial_generation_id, canonical_generation_id, pyramid_version, lifecycle_state, expected_systems, created_at, validated_at, published_at, failed_at, failure (first 240 chars or null)}.
(g) 'finder_products_on_published_generation': {system_search: <lifecycle_state or null>, system_archetype: <lifecycle_state or null>} for the CURRENT derived pointer's generation (both null when no pointer).
(h) 'migration_apply_preconditions': {'all_named_workers_stopped': bool, 'current_pointers_recorded': bool (true when sections c, d and f were all read without error), 'ready_for_governed_plan': bool = both}. This is reporting only.
Failures list codes exactly like the pattern: unexpected_host_identity, unexpected_working_directory, postgres_container_unavailable, postgres_runtime_identity_unavailable, read_only_query_failed (with 'query_error' holding the last stderr line, max 240 chars). Never print or read passwords, .env files, Config.Env, or any environment beyond the two identity names. Forbidden strings anywhere in the script: '.env', 'Config.Env', 'docker restart', 'docker compose up', 'docker compose down', 'docker stop', 'docker rm', 'systemctl', 'pg_dump', 'pg_restore', 'INSERT', 'UPDATE', 'DELETE', 'TRUNCATE', 'ALTER', 'DROP', 'CREATE', 'ADMIN_TOKEN', 'FRONTIER_CLIENT_SECRET', '/root/.ssh' (uppercase SQL keywords checked case-sensitively; the script only SELECTs). Add a top-of-file comment explaining in plain words what the action reports and that it is roadmap step 0 of the Finder rollout.
